title: Claude Sonnet 5.5: Anthropic Said Slow Down, Then Scheduled Two More
description: Sonnet 5.5 follows the pacing essay without breaking it, the gated Mythos is the same model as public Fable, and the leaked price is just Sonnet 5's current rate
imageAlt: Notebook sketch of Claude Sonnet 5.5 beside the pacing essay, Mythos equals Fable, and the rumored $2 / $10 price
body:
## 3-Line TL;DR

- Sonnet 5.5 does not break the pacing pledge as written, because Dario Amodei's essay defines pacing as slower capability gains with outside checks, not a release freeze
- The "hidden" model already has a public name: Mythos 5.1 is the same model as Fable 5.1, gated by safeguards, and Opus 5.5 already beats Fable 5.1 on every percentage benchmark Anthropic published
- The leaked Sonnet 5.5 price and context are Sonnet 5's current numbers, so wait for a model page and rerun your own tasks instead of switching on a rumor

## The slowdown essay came 10 days before the next release

![Timeline of 2026 Claude releases from Mythos Preview in April to Opus 5.5 on Sep 22, with the pacing essay on Sep 12](/media/93914099-fe8d-47a0-9544-605bfba7bf8f.webp)

*Sources: Anthropic announcements and the [Claude Opus 5.5 page](https://www.anthropic.com/claude-opus-5-5); essay date per Dario Amodei's post — chart by HSL*

- In September, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei wrote that "we must slow the pace at which we improve the capabilities of AI models" ([essay](https://darioamodei.com/post/we-must-pace-the-frontier))
- The same essay says pacing "does not mean halting model training or technical progress"
- It means taking "adequate time to align and safeguard" models and letting third-party evaluators confirm it
- Anthropic committed to the first step on its own: outside evaluators with permanent, employee-level access
- Opus 5.5 shipped on September 22 as the "first release since we called for pacing the frontier" ([Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/claude-opus-5-5))
- External evaluators, including Frontier Design and METR, tested it before release
- The same page says Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 "will follow in the coming weeks"
- The first release under the slowdown arrived with a schedule for two more
- That is not a betrayal of the essay, but the essay sets a much lower bar than the word "slow" suggests

## The Sonnet 5.5 leak reprinted Sonnet 5's price tag

| Item | Sonnet 5 (official) | Sonnet 5.5 (rumor) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Price per 1M tokens | $2 input / $10 output | $2 input / $10 output |
| Context window | 1M tokens | 872K to 1M tokens |
| Max output | 128K tokens | 128K tokens |
| Release | June 30, 2026 | "Next week," per leakers |

*Sources: [Anthropic models overview](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/overview) and [Sonnet 5 announcement](https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-sonnet-5); rumor from [TestingCatalog](https://www.testingcatalog.com/anthropic-claude-sonnet-5-5-release-date-leaks/), checked September 28, 2026*

- On September 27, leaker Lyra posted that partners had a second, improved Sonnet 5.5 checkpoint and a launch was near ([TestingCatalog](https://www.testingcatalog.com/anthropic-claude-sonnet-5-5-release-date-leaks/))
- The model name was reportedly seen on Factory, marked as not yet available
- An earlier September 24 "leak" listed 1M context, 128K output and $2 / $10 ([Startup Fortune](https://startupfortune.com/the-claude-sonnet-55-leak-beating-gpt-6-sol-is-not-what-it-looks-like/))
- Every one of those numbers was already on Sonnet 5's public spec sheet
- A leak that matches last quarter's price list is mostly a leak of the price list
- Anthropic's models page has no Sonnet 5.5 entry yet, so its price, scores and date are all unconfirmed
- Claims that it beats GPT-6 Sol come from testers' videos and posts, not a published evaluation

## The "hidden" top model already has a name: Mythos

![Bar chart of eight benchmarks where Opus 5.5 scores above Fable 5.1, from +0.6 to +10.6 points](/media/99ab7bdd-9624-4210-bf4e-7c8721d69bb1.webp)

*Source: [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/claude-opus-5-5) — Claude Opus 5.5 benchmark table, vendor-reported — chart by HSL*

- My guess was a ladder: Mythos and Fable on top, then Opus, then Sonnet, each distilled from the one above
- The official lineup is flatter than that
- "Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1 are the same model, but with different levels of safeguards" ([Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/claude-fable-and-mythos-5-1))
- Fable 5.1 is public at $10 / $50 per 1M tokens
- Mythos 5.1 is available only through trusted access programs for cyber defense and life sciences, currently for US organizations
- The model is the same, and the paperwork decides which version you get
- Opus 5.5 beats Fable 5.1 on all eight percentage benchmarks Anthropic lists, from 0.6 points on Chartography to 10.6 points on Terminal-Bench 4.0
- It also leads GDPval-AA v2.1, 1846 to 1735, at 60% lower per-token prices
- Anthropic says Opus 5.5 is "comparable to Claude Mythos 5.1 in biology and cybersecurity," so it ships with safeguards similar to Fable 5.1's
- Anthropic does not publish how its smaller models are trained, so "distilled from Mythos" stays my guess
- The distillation it does write about is the unauthorized kind: Opus 5.5 ships with preserved thinking, which it calls an "anti-distillation safeguard"
- Could an unreleased Fable 5.5 exist inside Anthropic? Nothing official says so
- The essay does list "internal use of AI to improve AI" as something pacing might limit, which is only worth limiting if it happens

## The essay itself calls frontier AI a security race

- The pacing essay is openly geopolitical, not only a safety memo
- It says pacing within democracies "will be limited by the lead that US companies have over authoritarian regimes, chiefly the Chinese Communist Party"
- Slow down more than that lead, it argues, and CCP-linked projects "will pull ahead, creating significant national security risk"
- It warns such a lead could let them "militarily dominate democracies (for example with AI-driven drones)"
- It also asks for a crackdown on "unauthorized distillation by companies in authoritarian countries"
- The Opus 5.5 page sums pacing up as keeping AI safe while "remaining competitive with China"
- The Mythos life sciences program runs "in partnership with the US government" ([Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/claude-fable-and-mythos-5-1))
- So "frontier AI as national strength and a weapon" is not a conspiracy reading
- It is the CEO's own framing, with the brake sized by the lead over China

## So what do I do when Sonnet 5.5 lands?

| Your situation | What I would do |
| :--- | :--- |
| Running Sonnet 5 in production | Wait for the model page, then rerun your own evals before switching the ID |
| Paying for Opus 5.5 on routine work | Test Sonnet 5.5 on the same prompts and compare cost per finished task |
| Paying $10 / $50 for Fable 5.1 | Check Opus 5.5 first, since it tops Fable 5.1 on every published row at 40% of the price |
| Hoping for Mythos access | Only if you are a vetted US organization in cyber defense or life sciences |
| Reading reasoning through the API | New accounts since August 31 get preserved thinking on Fable 5.1 and Opus 5.5 |

- Cheap per-token prices can still lose on the bill, as the [Astra vs Opus 5.5 same-prompt test](/en/posts/gpt-6-sol-luna-opus-5-5-cost-per-success/) showed

## Community Reactions

- An r/OpenAI commenter read the pacing essay as a request to slow rivals down until Anthropic caught up, a sarcastic interpretation of its timing ([Reddit](https://www.reddit.com/r/OpenAI/comments/1wee3nt/comment/p9cween/))
- In r/ClaudeAI, centminmod shared a CVP approval walkthrough, but the program text they quoted still described Mythos access as a future addition ([Reddit](https://www.reddit.com/r/ClaudeAI/comments/1w6sp4h/trusted_access_to_claude_mythos_51_fable_51/))

## Q&A (Field Notes)

- **Q. Is Sonnet 5.5 out yet?**
  - No, as of September 28, 2026 Anthropic has only said it will follow Opus 5.5 "in the coming weeks"
- **Q. Is Mythos a stronger model than Fable?**
  - No, Anthropic says they are the same model with different safeguards, and Mythos is the less restricted version for vetted organizations
- **Q. Does pacing mean Anthropic will release fewer models?**
  - Not by the essay's definition, which targets the speed of capability gains and adds outside checks rather than pausing releases
- **Q. Will Sonnet 5.5 cost more than Sonnet 5?**
  - Unknown, and the rumored $2 / $10 is simply Sonnet 5's current price
- **Q. Can I get Mythos 5.1 as an individual developer?**
  - Not currently, since access runs through trusted programs for organizations, currently limited to the US
